Vendored dependency: crossterm 0.29.0 (exact)
=============================================

Upstream project : crossterm-rs/crossterm
Upstream URL     : https://github.com/crossterm-rs/crossterm
crates.io release: 0.29.0 (published 2025-04-05; current stable 0.29 line)
Upstream commit  : 36d95b26a26e64b0f8c12edfe11f410a6d56a812 (tag "0.29")
License          : MIT (LICENSE file in this directory, unmodified)

Provenance
----------
Base tree: the crates.io-published 0.29.0 package as extracted by cargo
(copied from ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/
crossterm-0.29.0 on 2026-09-07). The package's .cargo_vcs_info.json pins
git sha1 36d95b26a26e64b0f8c12edfe11f410a6d56a812, verified equal to
refs/tags/0.29 via git ls-remote on 2026-09-07. Every file under src/ and
the LICENSE are byte-identical to the GitHub tag archive
(crossterm-0.29.tar.gz) modulo CRLF line terminators (the crates.io
package preserves CRLF as stored in the publishing checkout); verified
with a whole-tree `tr -d '\r' | diff` comparison.
This repository's `.gitattributes` (`* text eol=lf`) forces LF
normalization when this tree is staged or checked out, so the committed
blobs and any fresh checkout carry the LF variant of these files; the
checked-in bytes therefore differ from the extracted crates.io package
only by those same line terminators.
Upstream master as of 2026-09-07 is cdc30a9cd7f89d97a847c182feab66147eb50223
(verified via git ls-remote on 2026-09-07); this vendor tree is pinned to
the released 0.29.0 tag, not master.

Workspace wiring
----------------
The workspace root Cargo.toml carries:

    exclude = ["vendor/crossterm-0.29.0"]   (non-workspace vendor tree)

    [patch.crates-io]
    crossterm = { path = "vendor/crossterm-0.29.0" }

so every in-workspace crossterm 0.29.0 requirement (=0.29.0, exact pin in
crates/{pi,pi-ext,pi-tui}/Cargo.toml and ratatui 0.30.2 "crossterm_0_29")
resolves to this directory. The version, license, and upstream identity
are unchanged; this is a pinned-release local copy, not a fork.

Intentional prune (2026-09-07)
------------------------------
The upstream examples/ directory (11 files: ten example programs and their
README) and the ten [[example]] target declarations in this directory's
active Cargo.toml are removed. Reason: the repository's DOC-D ledger
invariant forbids any examples/ directory in the tree, and this vendored
crate is consumed only as a library (it is excluded from the workspace and
no build ever targets its examples). The original upstream manifest,
including the example declarations, is retained unmodified as
Cargo.toml.orig; every other recorded provenance property above is
unchanged.

Local modifications (persistent reply parser + typed reply collection)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
All local changes are marked with the comment tag "Vendored patch" and are
Unix byte-parser scoped; the Windows INPUT_RECORD source and all other
crossterm behavior are untouched. Files changed against upstream 0.29.0:

  src/event/source/unix/parser.rs  NEW - the ONE persistent byte parser
                              shared by both unix event sources. Holds any
                              `ESC`-opening candidate that could be an
                              OSC 11 reply header under an ABSOLUTE 50 ms
                              deadline (armed at the first ESC byte, never
                              reset by later bytes); recognizes the
                              `ESC ] 1 1 ;` header; carries payload/ST
                              fragments across arbitrary idle gaps and
                              timeouts once the header is recognized;
                              resolves diverging or expired pre-header
                              candidates through the existing `parse_event`
                              key decoder exactly once; latches an explicit
                              protocol error for recognized malformed or
                              oversized reply framing. Includes regression
                              tests with an injected clock.
  src/event/reply.rs          NEW - typed bounded reply sink (capacity 16,
                              drop-oldest) plus the ONE collection path:
                              poll_reply() drives the same shared reader and
                              parser every other consumer uses; drain_replies()
                              is a raw observation helper; recover_protocol_error()
                              and is_protocol_error() define session recovery.
                              Ordinary input seen while collecting stays
                              queued in the shared reader, in arrival order.
                              Cross-platform compile; active behavior is
                              unix-only.
  src/event.rs                `pub mod reply;` and the unix-only
                              `InternalEvent::ReplyConsumed` marker (a
                              sequence consumed into the reply sink; never
                              queued, so it never reaches filters or public
                              events).
  src/event/sys/unix/parse.rs cell-size reply recognition: `CSI 4 ; h ; w t`
                              and `CSI 6 ; h ; w t` push a typed reply to
                              the sink and return ReplyConsumed instead of
                              being dropped as unparsable key codes; and
                              cursor-position parsing (`CSI Cy ; Cx R`)
                              rejects a zero coordinate as a protocol
                              violation (could_not_parse_event_error)
                              instead of underflowing to 65535/panicking
                              on malformed replies like `CSI 0;0R`.
  src/event/source/unix/mio.rs   Uses the shared parser. try_read honors the
                              candidate deadline inside any caller wait,
                              surfaces the protocol error, and returns
                              promptly when a chunk completed a reply. The
                              ET drain is FAIRNESS-bounded, never
                              queue-bounded: a fresh edge latches a
                              persistent "tty readable" obligation that
                              survives every return; the drain runs in
                              windows of at most TTY_DRAIN_READ_BUDGET
                              reads, each read FIONREAD-guarded (so no
                              blocking read follows a short read on a
                              blocking fd, a short read is not a drained
                              proof while bytes remain queued, and
                              FIONREAD == 0 / WouldBlock / EOF are the
                              only drained proofs); wake/signal fds are
                              re-probed with a zero-timeout poll at every
                              window boundary; and the next call resumes
                              the drain without waiting for a new edge.
                              Source-level pipe tests include a
                              sustained-flood wake-budget witness, a
                              queued-tail-without-new-edge witness, and a
                              short-read-with-pending witness (libc cfg).
  src/event/source/unix/tty.rs   Same integration for the use-dev-tty
                              source, with the same tests.
  src/event/source.rs         EventSource::recover_protocol_error default
                              method.
  src/event/read.rs           InternalEventReader helpers for reply
                              collection (probe_try_read, queue_event,
                              take_queued_reply, recover_protocol_error).
  src/event/stream.rs         EventStream worker quiescence: shutdown check
                              before starting another poll, Err breaks the
                              worker loop instead of spinning (a latched
                              protocol error reaches the consumer as a
                              stream error), and Drop drops the task sender
                              and JOINS the wake thread, so after Drop
                              returns no worker can read the tty.

Behavior contract
-----------------
- One persistent parser owns every tty byte across startup probing,
  steady state, mid-session requeries, and pause/resume. There is no raw
  takeover, no staged-prefix transfer, and no application-side re-decoder;
  replies, partial CSI, UTF-8, and bracketed-paste state all live in the
  shared parser for the process lifetime.
- Escape framing (approved 50 ms policy): a lone `ESC` is ambiguous. The
  candidate is held under an absolute 50 ms deadline measured from the
  first ESC byte. Diverging input resolves immediately; an expired
  candidate resolves at the deadline into the exact ordinary key sequence
  (`ESC` -> Esc, `ESC ]` -> Alt+']', longer pre-header prefixes decode
  their held `1`/`;` suffix bytes as ordinary keys), each byte exactly
  once. Once `ESC ] 1 1 ;` is recognized the deadline is removed: payload
  and split ST fragments remain protocol across arbitrary idle gaps,
  consumer timeouts, and handoffs.
- Recognized, within-bound OSC 11 replies (`ESC ] 11 ; <payload> BEL|ESC \`,
  payload <= 64 bytes) are sunk to the typed reply queue and never decode
  as keys. The 63/64/65-byte payload boundaries behave identically at
  startup and steady state (63 and 64 complete; the 65th payload byte
  latches the error).
- Recognized malformed framing (ESC inside the payload not followed by
  `\`) or an oversized payload latches an explicit io::Error
  (ErrorKind::InvalidData, recognized by reply::is_protocol_error).
  Polls fail with it; NO payload byte is replayed as keys and no
  following input is silently discarded (the tty is simply not read while
  latched). Defined session recovery is reply::recover_protocol_error()
  (or an application pause+resume that calls it): the latch and partial
  framing state clear and decoding resumes fresh. The public Event enum
  has no error variant; the error surfaces through io paths only.
- Cell-size replies (`CSI 4 ; h ; w t`, `CSI 6 ; h ; w t`) are consumed
  into the typed sink; cursor position, kitty keyboard enhancement flags,
  and DA1 remain upstream InternalEvents and are additionally surfaced as
  typed replies through poll_reply. No new public Event variants.
- Bracketed paste is opaque to reply framing: paste content containing
  OSC-looking text stays literal input.
- Quiescence preconditions (NOT an all-timing guarantee): the framing
  deadline bounds ESC-ambiguity latency only. Collection and recovery
  APIs that drive the shared reader require the usual single-reader
  discipline: a caller may drive poll_reply/recover only while no other
  reader is polling — i.e. before the EventStream starts, or after the
  stream is paused (its worker dropped and joined, which EventStream::drop
  guarantees after its shutdown wake is honored — bounded reads (one per
  poll iteration in the use-dev-tty source, budget windows with control
  re-probes in the mio source) keep the worker responsive under a
  sustained reply flood). Within
  those windows there are no additional timing guarantees beyond the
  50 ms framing deadline and the callers' own explicit timeouts.

Why vendored
------------
Upstream 0.29.0 (and master as of 2026-09-07, HEAD
cdc30a9cd7f89d97a847c182feab66147eb50223) consumes no OSC color-query
replies and exposes no reader seam; an unknown OSC reply decodes as
Alt+']' plus character keys, which leaked terminal query payloads into
application input, and no upstream mechanism keeps reply framing distinct
from keyboard input across read partitions. The fix must live inside the
parser, so the exact released source is carried locally under the
upstream MIT license with provenance recorded here. No remote fork,
publication, or upstream PR is authorized or implied.
